The Holy Spirit has arranged Jeremiah's prophecies by the moral rather than the chronological connection. From the history of an event fifteen years before, the Jews, who had brought back their manumitted servants into bondage, are taught how much God loves and rewards obedience, and hates and punishes disobedience.<div eID="gen18501" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18502" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10371"/><hi type="bold">2. Rechabites--</hi>a nomadic tribe belonging to the Kenites of Hemath (<reference osisRef="1Chr.2.55">1Ch 2:55</reference>), of the family of Jethro, or Hobab, Moses' father-in-law (<reference osisRef="Exod.18.9">Ex 18:9</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="Num.10.29-Num.10.32">Nu 10:29-32</reference>; <reference osisRef="Judg.1.16">Jud 1:16</reference>). They came into Canaan with the Israelites, but, in order to preserve their independence, chose a life in tents without a fixed habitation (<reference osisRef="1Sam.15.6">1Sa 15:6</reference>). Besides the branch of them associated with Judah and extending to Amalek, there was another section at Kadesh, in Naphtali (<reference osisRef="Judg.4.11">Jud 4:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Judg.4.17">17</reference>). They seem to have been proselytes of the gate, Jonadab, son of Rechab, whose charge not to drink wine they so strictly obeyed, was zealous for God (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.10.15-2Kgs.10.23">2Ki 10:15-23</reference>). The Nabatheans of Arabia observed the same rules [Diodorus Siculus, 19.94].<div eID="gen18502" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18503" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bring ... into ... house of ... Lord--</hi>because there were suitable witnesses at hand there from among the priests and chief men, as also because he had the power immediately to address the people assembled there (<reference osisRef="Jer.35.13">Jr 35:13</reference>). It may have been also as a reproof of the priests, who drank wine freely, though commanded to refrain from it when in the discharge of their duties [Calvin].<div eID="gen18503" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18504" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">chambers--</hi>which were round about the temple, applied to various uses, for example, to contain the vestments, sacred vessels, &c. <div eID="gen18504" type="x-p"/>

The Nabatheans of Arabia observed the same rules [Diodorus Siculus, 19.94]. bring ... into ... house of ... Lord-- because there were suitable witnesses at hand there from among the priests and chief men, as also because he had the power immediately to address the people assembled there ( Jr 35:13 ). It may have been also as a reproof of the priests, who drank wine freely, though commanded to refrain from it when in the discharge of their duties [Calvin]. chambers-- which were round about the temple, applied to various uses, for example, to contain the vestments, sacred vessels, &c.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10373"/><div sID="gen18506" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10373"/><hi type="bold">4. man of God--</hi>a prophet (<reference osisRef="Deut.33.1">De 33:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.27">1Sa 2:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.22">1Ki 12:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.4.7">2Ki 4:7</reference>), also "a servant of God" in general (<reference osisRef="1Tim.6.11">1Ti 6:11</reference>), one not his own, but God's; one who has parted with all right in himself to give himself wholly to God (<reference osisRef="2Tim.3.17">2Ti 3:17</reference>). He was so reverenced that none would call in question what was transacted in his chamber.<div eID="gen18506" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18507" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">keeper of the door--</hi>Hebrew, "of the vessel." Probably the office meant is that of the priest who kept in charge the capitation money paid for the use of the temple and the votive offerings, such as silver vessels, &c. There were seven such keepers [Grotius]. Compare <reference osisRef="2Kgs.12.9">2Ki 12:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.18">25:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.18">1Ch 9:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.19">19</reference>, which support English Version.<div eID="gen18507" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18508" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I said ... Drink--</hi>Jeremiah does not say, The Lord saith, Drink: for then they would have been bound to obey. Contrast the case in <reference osisRef="1Kgs.13.7-1Kgs.13.26">1Ki 13:7-26</reference>. <div eID="gen18508" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10374"/><div sID="gen18509" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10374"/><hi type="bold">6. Jonadab ... our father--</hi>that is, forefather and director, three hundred years before (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.10.15">2Ki 10:15</reference>). They were called Rechabites, not Jonadabites, having received their name from Rechab the father, previously to their adopting the injunctions of Jonadab his son. This case affords no justification for slavish deference to the religious opinions of the Christian fathers: for Jonadab's injunction only affected matters of the present life; moreover, it was not binding on their consciences, for they deemed it not unlawful to go to Jerusalem in the invasion (<reference osisRef="Jer.35.11">Jr 35:11</reference>). What is praised here is not the father's injunction, but the obedience of the sons [Calvin]. <div eID="gen18509" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10377"/><div sID="gen18514" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10377"/><hi type="bold">11. Chaldeans ... Syrians--</hi>when Jehoiakim revolted from Nebuchadnezzar (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.24.1">2Ki 24:1</reference>, 2). Necessity sets aside all other laws. This is the Rechabites' excuse for their seeming disobedience to Jonadab in temporarily settling in a city. Herein was seen the prescient wisdom of Jonadab's commands; they could at a moment's notice migrate, having no land possessions to tie them. <div eID="gen18514" type="x-p"/>
